+- For rules160–162, `protected_manual` means that at least one declared `unit.fields` field has `fixed: true`, OR `about.field` is present and differs from `id`. A numeric unit cannot be a `worker.creates` target (the existing catalogue rule of P02.3). Physical retirement through `placement.retire_when.delete_after` or `placement.ends` is refused only for an **unprotected numeric** unit. `worker.deletes` is forbidden for **every numeric** unit, including a protected one. These are existing-class `refused:relations`; there is no schema/view change. Named units keep their existing rules. The distinct unplaced rule49 below is unchanged (the Architect's ADR-0127 P/06 C3 decision).
- `placement.unplaced.delete_after` no longer requires the absence of `fixed` fields and of `about` by id (rules 46–47 in the former numbering, before ADR-0091, are
removed, the amendment of ADR-0067 addendum 2026-10-10 by the decision of ADR-0091 item 1): for a table with such fields
the controller physically deletes only the rows with `made` (P/04 N1.3), the manual ones it takes off without deleting;

`$INSTANCE_ID` is the existing common instance override: absent or empty selects the ordinary box/pid/random resolver; a supplied nonempty value is accepted or refused by the instance contract and preserved byte for byte. It is environment, with no new CLI flag or new configuration rule.

[runtime-constants.tsv](runtime-constants.tsv) is the numeric source of its 25 declared constants. Header is `name value unit norm meaning`, literal TAB. Name is unique `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`; value is a positive JSON integer, no quotes; unit is `count|s|bytes`; norm is an existing req anchor of its owning chapter; meaning is text. No expression language or new environment knob is introduced. The cited procedure owns dependent formulas and conditional use: in particular OPS_KEEP cannot undercut the subsystem acceptance-memory term. These literals may be emitted with core; they do not declare a wholly generated stage.
